unwrap.title: How Result::unwrap works
unwrap.description: Takes the value out of Ok; panics with the error for Err.

note.text: fine for Ok, a crash for Err

slides.caption: unwrap assumes success. An Err stops the program and prints the error.
Ok(4): the 4 comes out.
Err("bad"): panic with called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: "bad".
In functions that return Result, use ? instead: it passes the error up to the caller.

expect.title: How Result::expect works
expect.description: Like unwrap, with your own message in the panic.

title.text: ok.expect("value must be ok"), err.expect("value must be ok")

slides.caption: expect behaves like unwrap but starts the panic message with your text.
Ok: the value comes out.
Err: the program stops with your message followed by the error.
Good for things that can only fail through a bug or broken setup, with a message that says what.

unwrap_or.title: How Result::unwrap_or works
unwrap_or.description: The value for Ok, a default for Err (the error is ignored).

slides.caption: unwrap_or replaces any error with the default.
Err("bad"): the error is dropped and 0 is used.
The error is lost. If it matters, log it or use match / ?.

unwrap_or_else.title: How Result::unwrap_or_else works
unwrap_or_else.description: The value, or a closure that gets the error and returns a fallback.

slides.caption: unwrap_or_else calls the closure with the error, only for Err.
Ok(4): 4, the closure is not called.
Err("bad"): the closure gets "bad" and returns its length, 3.
Useful to log the error and continue with a fallback value.

map.title: How Result::map works
map.description: Changes the Ok value; an Err passes through untouched.

slides.caption: map transforms success values and leaves errors alone.
Err("bad") is passed on unchanged; the closure is not called.
map_err is the mirror image: it changes the error and leaves Ok alone.

map_err.title: How Result::map_err works
map_err.description: Changes the error; an Ok passes through untouched.

slides.caption: map_err is used to turn one error type into another, often to add context.
Ok(4) stays Ok(4).
Err("bad") becomes Err("config: bad").
Typical before ?: file.read().map_err(MyError::Io)?.

and_then.title: How Result::and_then works
and_then.description: Runs the next step only on success; that step may fail too.

slides.caption: and_then chains steps that each return a Result. The first Err stops the chain.
"8" parses to 8, and half(8) is Ok(4).
"7" parses, but half(7) fails: Err("odd").
"x" does not parse: Err("nan"), and half is never called.
Inside a function, the ? operator usually reads better than long and_then chains.

ok.title: How Result::ok works
ok.description: Turns a Result into an Option, throwing the error away.

slides.caption: ok() keeps the success value and forgets the error.
Ok(4) becomes Some(4).
Err("bad") becomes None: the error message is gone.
Common with filter_map: lines.filter_map(|l| l.parse().ok()) keeps only the lines that parse.

is_ok.title: How Result::is_ok works
is_ok.description: true for Ok, false for Err.

slides.caption: is_ok tells you whether it worked, without taking anything out.
Ok(4): true.
Err("bad"): false. is_err() is the opposite.
To use the value too, write if let Ok(v) = result { ... } or match.

unwrap_or_default.title: How Result::unwrap_or_default works
unwrap_or_default.description: The value, or the type's default for Err.

slides.caption: unwrap_or_default uses the default value of the type when there is an error.
Err: 0, the default i32.
For String the default is "", for Vec an empty Vec, for bool false.

or_else.title: How Result::or_else works
or_else.description: On Err, tries an alternative that may also fail.

slides.caption: or_else calls the closure only for Err, and uses its Result instead.
The first read worked: its Ok is kept, the closure never runs.
The first read failed: the closure tries the default, which works.
If the fallback fails too, its Err is returned.

err.title: How Result::err works
err.description: Turns a Result into an Option of the error.

slides.caption: err() keeps only the error side.
Ok(4) has no error: None.
Err("bad") gives Some("bad").
Handy for collecting just the failures: results.iter().filter_map(|r| r.as_ref().err()).
is_err tells you whether there is an error, without looking at it.
"x" is not a number: parse returns Err.
is_err() is true.
To see the error, use if let Err(e) = result.

map_or.title: How Result::map_or works
map_or.description: Applies a closure to Ok, or returns a default for Err.

slides.caption: map_or gives f(value) for Ok, and the default for Err.
Err: the default, 0.
The error is ignored. map_or_else(|e| ..., f) lets you use it.

unwrap_err.title: How Result::unwrap_err works
unwrap_err.description: Takes the error out of Err; panics on Ok.

slides.caption: unwrap_err is unwrap for the error side: you expect a failure.
The parse failed, so the error comes out.
On Ok it would panic instead.
Mostly used in tests to check that something fails, and why.

is_ok_and.title: How Result::is_ok_and works
is_ok_and.description: true if it is Ok and the value passes the test.

slides.caption: One call answers "did it work, and is the value right?".
"-1": Ok, but not positive.
"x": Err.
is_err_and does the same for the error side.

and.title: How Result::and works
and.description: If Ok, gives the second Result; an Err is kept.

slides.caption: and returns the second Result only when the first succeeded.
Ok, so the result is the second: Ok("x").
The first failed: its Err("a") is returned.
and_then takes a closure that receives the Ok value.

or.title: How Result::or works
or.description: Keeps Ok; replaces an Err with another Result.

slides.caption: or keeps a success and swaps a failure for the fallback.
Ok(1) is kept.
Err("a") is replaced by Ok(9).
or_else takes a closure that receives the error.

map_or_else.title: How Result::map_or_else works
map_or_else.description: One closure for the error, one for the value.

slides.caption: map_or_else(on_err, on_ok) turns either case into the same type.
Ok(4): on_ok gives 8.
Err("bad"): on_err gives its length, 3.
The error closure comes first in the argument list.

inspect_err.title: How Result::inspect_err works
inspect_err.description: Looks at the error (for logging) and passes the Result on.

slides.caption: inspect_err runs only for Err and does not change the Result.
Ok: the closure is skipped.
Err: the closure logs it; the Err continues to ?.
Keeps error logging out of the main flow of the code.

transpose.title: How Result::transpose works
transpose.description: Turns Result<Option<T>, E> into Option<Result<T, E>>.

slides.caption: transpose moves the Option to the outside.
Ok(Some(4)) becomes Some(Ok(4)).
Ok(None) becomes None.
Err stays an error: Some(Err("e")).
Useful inside filter_map, which wants an Option.
map on a Result consumes it. as_ref first turns it into references, so the original stays.
as_ref lends the String.
map reads its length: 2.
as_mut gives mutable references instead.

as_mut.title: How Result::as_mut works
as_mut.description: Lends the contents mutably: &mut Result<T, E> → Result<&mut T, &mut E>.

slides.caption: as_mut lets you change the Ok (or Err) value without moving it out.
Ok(1) becomes Ok(2).
An Err is left alone here.
Same idea as Option::as_mut.

iter.title: How Result::iter works
iter.description: An iterator over the Ok value: one item for Ok, none for Err.

slides.caption: iter treats Ok(v) as [v] and Err as [].
Ok(3) yields 3.
Err yields nothing.
Iterating a list of Results with flatten() keeps only the Ok values.

inspect.title: How Result::inspect works
inspect.description: Looks at the Ok value (for logging) and passes the Result on unchanged.

slides.caption: inspect only runs the closure for Ok and returns the same Result.
The text parses to Ok(42).
inspect sees 42 (and could log it).
The chain continues untouched.
inspect_err does the same for errors.

expect_err.title: How Result::expect_err works
expect_err.description: Gets the error out; panics with your message if it was Ok.

slides.caption: expect_err is expect for the error side, mostly used in tests.
Err("boom") gives "boom".
Ok(1) would panic with the message.
unwrap_err does the same with a generic message.

is_err_and.title: How Result::is_err_and works
is_err_and.description: true if it is an Err and the error passes the test.

slides.caption: is_err_and combines is_err() with a check of the error value.
Err(404): true.
Err(500) fails the test: false.
Ok is never true here.
is_ok_and is the Ok-side twin.

copied.title: How Result::copied works
copied.description: Result<&T, E> → Result<T, E> by copying the value.

slides.caption: copied works for Copy types like numbers.
Ok holds a reference to 5.
copied gives Ok(5) itself.
cloned does the same for types that are Clone but not Copy.

cloned.title: How Result::cloned works
cloned.description: Result<&T, E> → Result<T, E> by cloning the value.

slides.caption: cloned calls clone() on the borrowed value.
Ok holds &String.
cloned gives an owned String.
Use it when the Result must outlive the borrowed collection.
as_deref borrows the Ok value through Deref, so a String becomes &str.
Ok(String) becomes Ok(&str).
Now it compares with a literal.
Same idea as Option::as_deref.

into_iter.title: How Result::into_iter works
into_iter.description: Consumes the Result: one item for Ok, none for Err.

slides.caption: flatten() uses each Result's into_iter, so Errs simply disappear.
Ok(1) yields 1.
Err yields nothing.
Ok(3) yields 3.
To stop at the first error instead, collect into Result<Vec<_>, _>.

iter_mut.title: How Result::iter_mut works
iter_mut.description: A mutable iterator over the Ok value (0 or 1 items).

slides.caption: For Err the loop body never runs.
The Ok value is 10.
It becomes 11.
if let Ok(v) = &mut r is usually clearer.
Borrow the Ok value mutably through its Deref target.
The String is lent as &mut str.
Upper-cased in place.
as_deref is the read-only version.
The first error, inner or outer, wins.
Inner error → Err("b").
Outer error → Err("a").
Same as .and_then(|r| r).

unwrap_unchecked.title: How Result::unwrap_unchecked works
unwrap_unchecked.description: Takes the Ok value without checking (unsafe).

slides.caption: On Err it is undefined behaviour.
Skip the check.
Use ? or unwrap normally.

unwrap_err_unchecked.title: How Result::unwrap_err_unchecked works
unwrap_err_unchecked.description: Takes the Err value without checking (unsafe).

slides.caption: On Ok it is undefined behaviour.
Skip the check.
unwrap_err() checks.

map_or_default.title: How Result::map_or_default works
map_or_default.description: Maps Ok(x), or returns the default value for Err.

slides.caption: The error itself is discarded.
Ok: 8.
Err: 0.
unwrap_or_default after map does the same.
